newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares show no sign of giving up steam.
newsitem.headline: German shares show no sign of giving up steam.

text.p: The German share market showed little sign of running out of power in the near-term after the DAX index surged to another record high on Friday, underpinned by the firmer dollar and Wall Street gains.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 36.45 points at 3,744.44 points after setting another record high at 3,751.26 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was steady in post-bourse trade at 3,744.49 points.
Some traders said the market, however, may need a brief pause before a run at higher levels, including the DAX index seeking to break 4,000 points.
"The market needs a bit of break at these levels," said one Frankfurt trader, who noted the DAX index has outperformed the Dow Jones index in 1997. "But this rally isn't over yet."
The Dow Jones index has risen about 20 percent, or about 1,260 points, since the start of the year, while the DAX index has rise about 30 percent, or 900 points.
"It's questionable whether these types of gains can be upheld," said another bourse trader on Friday.
Market attention next week will remain focused on Wall Street and also Monday's European Union summit in Amsterdam and the French-German clash over the future of the euro.
"Next week is going to be a test of whether the Dow can reach 8,000 points and the DAX can reach 4,000 points," said one Frankfurt trader. "It may turn into a struggle."

Among specific shares, SGL Carbon rose 9.60 marks to 243.10 marks, recovering after falling earlier this week when U.S. and European Union officials said they were probing SGL for possible price-fixing allegations.
